subject.title: fix: restore GitHub Copilot turns and account context limits

question: Should OpenClaw accept this broad shared-runtime implementation for the GitHub Copilot fix after the branch is refreshed and its exact merge result is reviewed?
rationale: The implementation is proof-positive and has no concrete remaining defect, but it modifies shared authentication, transport, compaction, media, and persisted-cache boundaries that require owner acceptance rather than automated repair.

options.title: Refresh and approve
options.body: Refresh onto current main, clear or attribute the two failing gates, and approve the exact merge result if the credential-scoped invariants remain intact.

options.title: Narrow shared scope
options.body: Retain the Copilot fix but remove shared media or compaction changes that cannot be justified and proven on the refreshed head.

options.title: Pause landing
options.body: Hold the PR until provider and agent-runtime owners can validate multi-account and upgrade behavior.

recommendation.title: Refresh and approve
recommendation.body: Refresh onto current main, clear or attribute the two failing gates, and approve the exact merge result if the credential-scoped invariants remain intact.

likelyOwner.reason: This person merged the two central provider changes, is already mentioned in the discussion, and is the strongest available owner for the cross-boundary merge choice.
